stories.title: Murder probe launched after woman found dead in Limerick
stories.summary: Gardaí have launched a murder investigation following the discovery of a women's body in Limerick city. The woman's body was found yesterday morning in an apartment on Lower Cecil Street. She has been named locally as Brazilian woman Jady Cristine Pereira Rosa, who was in her 30s. Her body was removed from the scene to the mortuary in University Hospital Limerick, where a post-mortem examination was carried out by the State Pathologist.

stories.title: TikTok declines Oireachtas call to discuss driving videos
stories.summary: Social media giant TikTok has declined an invitation to appear before the Oireachtas Committee on Media to discuss the posting of videos of people driving down motorways the wrong way and endangering other people's lives. In a response to a meeting request, a TikTok spokesperson said they cannot attend because of the ongoing garda investigation, a separate examination by Coimisiún na Meán and the fact they are the only company to have been asked to attend. Yesterday, Labour TD and media committee chair Alan Kelly wrote to TikTok requesting that its officials attend a meeting next month to discuss the situation and what he described as "content that glorifies irresponsible or illegal activity". "As a result, we believe it would not be possible to appear before the committee in public session until this process is completed.

stories.title: Canadian PM slams trade 'war' launched by US
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney today slammed what he called a trade "war" launched by the United States after the neighbours failed to reach an agreement, leading to the imposition of stiff US tariffs. "You're at war when you get attacked. We got attacked," Mr Carney told reporters this afternoon after the US said it would impose 50% tariffs on some imports from Canada. A senior US administration official said Section 338 tariffs on about $20 billion (€17bn) worth of Canadian goods would go into effect just after midnight (5am Irish time). Mr Carney said that he had suspended the trade negotiations and would retaliate ‌dollar for dollar, with Canadian tariffs taking effect on 8 September.

stories.title: Two dead in Croatia small plane crash
stories.summary: Two people were found dead late last night after a small plane flying from the Czech Republic crashed close to the coastal city of Zadar, Croatia, the authorities said. According to the Croatian police, a search was launched after air traffic control sounded the alarm that the plane's signal was lost at around 4pm (3pm Ireland time). The remains of the plane were found in the mountains of the Paklenica national park some 60 kilometres northeast of Zadar. "The search for the missing ultralight plane was concluded around 10pm when members of the Croatian Mountain Rescue Service found the plane and two dead persons," the police said in a statement.

stories.title: McIlroy reignites BMW Championship hopes
stories.summary: Rory McIlroy pulled himself back into contention at the BMW Championship with a strong finish for a five-under-par third round in St Louis, leaving him five shots behind leader Wyndham Clark. McIlroy has been looking for a response after labouring to an eight-over finish at last week's St Jude Championship, and shot a fine six-under opening round for a share of the lead, before following that up with a 69 on Friday. The back-to-back Masters champion again appeared in steady form during the front nine on Saturday, turning at one under after a birdie on the par-three second before another on 11. World number two McIlroy then stepped things up with a run of four birdies from the 13th, sandwiched by a bogey at the 14th.

stories.title: McCartan: Newbies brought 'freshness' to Cork panel
stories.summary: After being in the last six All-Ireland camogie finals and winning three of those, it may have been difficult to change a winning formula. Getting to so many successive finals prove that Cork camogie has clearly been in a golden age. But this season saw a lot of change in the Cork camp. After a very difficult start, forward Sorcha McCartan credited a "freshness" that the new players brought into the senior camogie set up during the season just gone. "I think they brought a bit of a freshness in terms of maybe there was less of a tense atmosphere. Not that the girls that left were tense, but I suppose they were around for so long that they brought a bit of seriousness to it. "They understood the magnitude of trouble that we were in. We had one win on the board at the end of May. That's really unheard of for a Cork camogie team.

stories.title: World Rugby loses bid to throw out concussion lawsuits
stories.summary: Hundreds of claims against rugby's governing bodies from players who allege they suffered brain injuries during their careers can continue to trial, the London High Court has ruled. World Rugby, Welsh Rugby, the Rugby Football Union, the Rugby Football League and the British Amateur Rugby League Association told a hearing last month that about 500 claims should be thrown out before trial for their lawyers’ failure to comply with court orders. The cases are part of a larger group filed by a mix of professional and amateur players, who claim the bodies breached a duty of care to protect them from injury. Their lawyers say they have suffered neurological injuries such as early-onset dementia, Parkinson’s, epilepsy and motor neurone disease because of repeated blows suffered throughout their sporting lives.

The Goat Exchange, the New York company behind the production, said: "The Goat Exchange regrets to announce that Ruth Negga will be stepping back from Radio Bette. In a statement, The Dublin Theatre Festival said that Radio Bette will go ahead as planned, with a replacement cast member to be announced 'in the next seven to 10 days'.

stories.title: Irish excise on alcohol second highest in Europe - study
stories.summary: Irish consumers pay the second highest excise duty on alcohol in Europe, according to new research. The research from Dublin City University economist Anthony Foley, commissioned by the Drinks Industry Group of Ireland (DIGI), shows that Ireland comes only behind Finland when it comes to excise levies on alcohol. When broken down by type of alcoholic drink, excise on wine in Ireland is the second highest in the EU and UK, also behind Finland, while excise on beer and spirits is the third highest, behind Finland and Sweden. A pint of beer purchased in a pub here attracts an excise duty of €0.55 compared to just €0.05 in Spain and Germany.

stories.title: Wholesale electricity prices up 56% in 12 months to July
stories.summary: New figures from the Central Statistics Office show that wholesale electricity prices rose by 14.8% in July when compared with June and were 56.2% higher than July of last year. While wholesale electricity prices remain 59.9% lower when compared with their peak in August 2022, they reached their highest level since January 2025 last month. The CSO said that all Energy Fuels were up by 0.6% in the month and were up 19.1% since July of last year. Commenting on today's CSO figures, price comparison website Bonkers.ie said that looking at the past six months, which gives a better indication of underlying trends, wholesale electricity prices were almost 30% higher than in the previous six-month period.

stories.title: Trump tariffs cool Quebec's push for independence for now
stories.summary: When US President Donald Trump levied 50% tariffs on Canadian steel in June last year, a steel factory in Canada's mostly French-speaking province of Quebec lost about a third of its orders for bolts and fasteners in less than a week. The factory owner, The Heico Companies, froze hiring, closed a plant in the region and laid off several dozen people, said David Jeannotte, an operations director, whose own brother lost his job. The cuts were part of 140 layoffs by the company, mainly in Quebec. The factory's troubles reflect broader anxiety over the fallout from Mr Trump's trade war in Quebec, which is due to hold a provincial election by 5 October. But while some previous economic slowdowns in the province prompted an increase in separatist sentiment, polls show that this time around, support for an independent Quebec is at its lowest level in decades, at about 30%.

stories.title: Feely already dreaming of scaling senior heights in 2027
stories.summary: While the achievements of this year are still very fresh in her mind, Roscommon's Aisling Feely is eagerly anticipating the prospect of playing senior championship football in 2027. Courtesy of their emphatic 2-12 to 0-06 triumph over Fermanagh in the TG4 All-Ireland intermediate football championship decider at Croke Park on 2 August, the Rossies will be one of 12 counties to feature in the top-tier of the LGFA next summer. Even before taking part in the race for the Brendan Martin Cup, the primrose and blue will lock horns with newly-crowned All-Ireland senior winners Galway and Mayo in next year’s Connacht championship at the highest grade of ladies football. This will help to make it a three-team series out in the west once again, as it was when the previous season’s All-Ireland intermediate champions Leitrim made the brief step up to senior football in 2025, and Feely is excited about this new opportunity for Roscommon. "We saw Leitrim do it two years ago. We would have been always there or thereabouts with them. They knocked us out in the quarter-final that year by two points and they went on to win it. That gave us a bit of inspiration. If Leitrim can do it, why can’t we. We’re just as good. To get up to senior is absolutely massive," Feely acknowledged.

stories.title: Kelly urges TikTok to reconsider committee invitation
stories.summary: Labour TD and chair of the Oireachtas committee on media Alan Kelly has responded to TikTok's decision to reject an invite to the committee to discuss the posting of illegal criminal videos by saying the platform, Google, Meta and X must now attend. On Wednesday, Mr Kelly wrote to TikTok raising significant concerns over the posting of videos of people driving the wrong way down motorways, and other illegal activity, on the platform. TikTok declined the invite yesterday, saying it feels it cannot attend due to the ongoing garda investigation into Sunday's M9 motorway crash and a Coimisiún na Meán examination of social media content relating to the incident. The social media giant also said it did not feel it would be appropriate for it to be the only platform to attend a media committee meeting on the issue, but added it would be happy to consider a private meeting.

stories.title: Building of over 3,000 homes commenced in July
stories.summary: The building of 3,028 new homes was commenced in July - an increase of 169% on the same month last year (1,125) - according to figures to be published later today by the Department of Housing. Of the new commencements last month, over half (1,612) are houses being built as part of multi-unit developments, 1,004 are apartments, with the remaining 412 made up of one-off houses. The department said that since the beginning of 2026, 18,974 new homes have been commenced, which is up 152% from the 7,539 homes commenced in the first seven months of last year. The data show it is also the second highest number of new-home commencements for the period, since recording began in 2014.

stories.title: UK retail sales soften in July after June World Cup boost
stories.summary: British retail sales fell back as expected in July after a surge in June when hot weather boosted demand for fans and air conditioners and supermarkets offered promotions alongside the men's soccer World Cup, official figures showed today. UK retail sales volumes last month dropped 0.5% from June, in line with economists' median forecast in a Reuters poll. Annual sales growth slowed to 1.6% in July from a downwardly revised 3.8%, slightly below expectations for a fall to 2.2%. The biggest drag came from clothing and footwear sales, which fell by the most since May 2025, down 2.7% on the month, after many stores began summer sales in June rather than July.

stories.title: Athlone reach fifth final in a row after shoot-out joy
stories.summary: Holders Athlone Town made it an incredible five FAI Cup finals in a row as they eventually overcame a gutsy Galway United on penalties, to set up a showdown with title rivals Shelbourne for the fourth time in that run of deciders. Alexis Strickland gave her side a dream start after nine minutes only to see her goal cancelled out by a stunning Cara Griffin leveller. But it was Maria Matthaiou who stood tall to save the decisive penalty after 120-plus minutes of action brought no winner. Despite the absence of top goalscorer Emma Doherty, who has bagged 14 in all competitions, and Remini Tillotson due to suspension, there was a confidence in the visitors' dressing room having been the only team to taste victory over Lily Agg's juggernaut and proved yet again to be more than just a thorn in their side.

stories.title: Kobe-mania and the Irish experiment
stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.
